## Summary

Lynda Blanchard was confirmed to be US ambassador to United Nations Agencies for Food and Agriculture, with confirmation occurring in a Senate vote with a 51-47 result on October 7, 2025. She assumed office on November 10, 2025 under President Donald Trump.

Blanchard was nominated to serve as ambassador for the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in Rome. She was previously confirmed by the Senate in 2019 as U.S. ambassador to Slovenia from 2019 to 2021.

## Summary of Results

Lynda Blanchard was nominated by President Donald Trump to serve as the United States ambassador to the United Nations Agencies for Food and Agriculture, headquartered in Rome, Italy.

The Senate Foreign Affairs Committee advanced Blanchard's nomination with an 11-10 party-line vote in September 2025. The full U.S. Senate voted 51-47 along partisan lines to approve Blanchard to be U.S. Representative to the United Nations Agencies for Food and Agriculture, with the rank of ambassador, and she assumed office on November 10, 2025.

Blanchard, a Montgomery native, formerly served as U.S. Ambassador to Slovenia and co-founded the 100x Development Foundation. This represents her return to diplomatic service during Trump's second term in office.
